Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Civic life: news, government & the law

speech noun

a talk given to an audience

also address, give a speech, make a speech, deliver a speech, oration

classical

Cic. Brut. 91: scrībuntur ōrātiōnēs habitae jam
Traupman 176: ōrātiōnem habēre, give a speech
Traupman 302: (ōrātiōnem) habēre

ōrātiō, ōrātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a speech

Ōrātiōnem habēre, to give a speech. Lewis & Short: “a set speech”, as against sermō, ordinary talk.

Other words

  • contiō, contiōnis f. — a speech to a public meeting; the meeting itself

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 9.14.7: lēgī enim contiōnem tuam; Cic. Att. 7.8.5: Antōnī contiōnem habitam

    An address to the people or to an army, called together by a magistrate or a general.

  • verba facere — speak, make a speech (to a gathering)

    verbum, verbī n., with faciō, facere, fēcī, factum · also used · classical · Caes. BG 2.14.1 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • sed quid agō? paene ōrātiōnem in epistulam inclūsī.

    But what am I doing? I’ve nearly put a whole speech into a letter.Cic. Att. 1.16.10

  • plēraeque enim scrībuntur ōrātiōnēs habitae jam, nōn ut habeantur

    for most speeches are written down once they have been given, not in order to be givenCic. Brut. 91

See also speech, address, debate, talk.
